Subject: Renewal proposal — hybrid co-term & staged uptake

Hi Elena / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the productive renewal discussion last week. Per our call I attached a lightweight term sheet that aligns Acme's three existing product lines onto a co-termed schedule while giving you a staged capacity uplift across Q1–Q4 of year one. The intent is to: 

- Co-term the contracts to simplify billing and reporting (single renewal date Jan 1, 2027)
- Provide a 24-month term on the master agreement with a staged capacity ramp (20% quarter-over-quarter in year 1)
- Keep an auto-renew clause at the master level but allow the usage buckets to be adjusted with 60-day notice

Key asks from our side:
1) Agreement on the co-term target (Jan 1, 2027)
2) Confirmation that staged uplift (Q1 baseline, then +20% QoQ) is operationally acceptable
3) Procurement and legal feedback on the attached term sheet by EOD next Tue (25 Aug) so we can get DocuSign out the following week

Attached: Acme_Renewal_TermSheet_v3.pdf (term sheet with staged capacity table) and RDW_SOW_redwood_uplift.xlsx (detailed ramp & onboarding milestones).

If you'd like, we can jump on a 30m call to walk through the ramp schedule with CS and Engineering.

Best,

Irene / team,

Quick take from finance: proposal below is conservative and reduces short-term exposure while keeping upsell mechanics intact. 

- Q1 soft cap at 120% of baseline monthly usage; any consumption between 120–150% will be invoiced at standard rate but 50% of excess will be applied as a credit to Q2 billing (credit applied only once). Consumption above 150% billed at list with no credit.
- Maintain monthly billing cadence but include a one-line billing memo showing "soft cap credit" when applied.
- We can accept a 30-day pre-renew review clause if it's explicit that cancellation within that window requires written notice to avoid unintended restart of services. Otherwise fine.

If legal wants stricter termination rights we'll need to route to contracts, but functionally this gives Acme comfort while protecting Redwood economics. Happy to draft the overage paragraph for the term sheet.

Sergio

Elena / team — attaching the revised term sheet and SOW with the changes we discussed. Highlights below: 

- Master term: 24 months (01-Jan-2027 through 12-Dec-2028) with a 30-day pre-renew review window; auto-renew will proceed only if we receive no written cancellation notice within that 30-day window.
- Q1 soft cap: 120% baseline with a crediting ladder (120–150% = half credit applied to next quarter; >150% billed at list). Full paragraph is in the attached "RDW_SOW_redwood_uplift.xlsx" tab 'Billing'.
- Co-term: all three lines consolidated to Jan 1 renewal to simplify invoicing and reporting.

Next steps: please review attachments and confirm (1) acceptance of the soft-cap credit approach, (2) DocuSign week-of-Sept 7 availability, and (3) any redlines from your legal team. If those are aligned we'll prepare the DocuSign package and route through HubSpot for deal close.
